'''Gennadi Milinevsky''' is a Ukrainian atmosphere scientist and a professor of physics and mathematics at [[Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv]] (KNU). He is a professor at the International Center for Future Science within the College of Physics at [[Jilin University]] (JLU)<ref name=faw/> and holds a position as principal scientist at the Main Astronomical Observatory of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]] (NAS).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uac.gov.ua/about/team/milinevskij/|title=Міліневський Геннадій Петрович, старший науковий співробітник}}</ref>

Milinevsky's primary research interest lies in atmospheric studies, particularly focusing on [[climate change]] processes and their effects on [[ecosystem]]s. He has participated in Antarctic expeditions and contributed to Antarctic scientific research, researching the effects of ozone hole dynamics on the Antarctic ecosystem and the impact of [[radioactive contamination]] on the environment.<ref name=ble>{{Cite web|url=http://www.antarcticfund.org/the-science-advisory-group-1|title=ADVISORY GROUP|website=AWR}}</ref> He has published over 100 papers in scientific journals, including ''[[Climate Dynamics]]'',<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00382-021-05886-7|title=The 16-year periodicity in the winter surface temperature variations in the Antarctic Peninsula region|first1=Oleksandr|last1=Evtushevsky|first2=Asen|last2=Grytsai|first3=Oleksiy|last3=Agapitov|first4=Volodymyr|last4=Kravchenko|first5=Gennadi|last5=Milinevsky|date=January 1, 2022|journal=Climate Dynamics|volume=58|issue=1|pages=35–47|via=Springer Link|doi=10.1007/s00382-021-05886-7|bibcode=2022ClDy...58...35E |url-access=subscription}}</ref> ''Journal of Southern Hemisphere Earth Systems Science'',<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.publish.csiro.au/es/ES19019|title=The Antarctic ozone hole during 2017|first1=Andrew R.|last1=Klekociuk|first2=Matthew B.|last2=Tully|first3=Paul B.|last3=Krummel|first4=Oleksandr|last4=Evtushevsky|first5=Volodymyr|last5=Kravchenko|first6=Stuart I.|last6=Henderson|first7=Simon P.|last7=Alexander|first8=Richard R.|last8=Querel|first9=Sylvia|last9=Nichol|first10=Dan|last10=Smale|first11=Gennadi P.|last11=Milinevsky|first12=Asen|last12=Grytsai|first13=Paul J.|last13=Fraser|first14=Zheng|last14=Xiangdong|first15=H. Peter|last15=Gies|first16=Robyn|last16=Schofield|first17=Jonathan D.|last17=Shanklin|date=June 11, 2020|journal=Journal of Southern Hemisphere Earth Systems Science|volume=69|issue=1|pages=29–51|via=www.publish.csiro.au|doi=10.1071/ES19019|doi-access=free}}</ref> and ''[[Antarctic Science]]''. He is the recipient of Fedorov Award from the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine and Medals "For Service" II Stage and III Stage from the [[Government of Ukraine]].<ref name=rrr>{{Cite web|url=http://uac.gov.ua/en/on-the-day-of-the-25th-anniversary-of-akademik-vernadsky-station-ukrainian-polar-explorers-received-state-awards-from-the-president/|title=On the day of the 25th anniversary of Akademik Vernadsky station, Ukrainian polar explorers received state awards from the President|date=February 6, 2021}}</ref>

Milinevsky has been a member of the [[American Geophysical Union]] (AGU) since 1990 and the [[European Geosciences Union]] (EGU) since 2012. He holds the position of executive editor for the ''Ukrainian Antarctic Journal''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://uaj.uac.gov.ua/index.php/uaj/about/editorialTeam|title=Editorial Team &#124; Ukrainian Antarctic Journal|website=uaj.uac.gov.ua}}</ref> and associate editor for the ''Frontiers in Remote Sensing''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mdpi.com/journal/remotesensing/announcements/7838|title=Remote Sensing|website=www.mdpi.com}}</ref>

==Education and early career==
Milinevsky earned his M.S. degree in [[astronomy]] and [[astrophysics]] from Kyiv State University in 1974, followed by a Ph.D. in geophysics from the Institute of Geophysics in 1980.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://science.knu.ua/en/researchgroups/research.php?ELEMENT_ID=2665|title=Gennadi Milinevsky|website=science.knu.ua}}</ref> He held the role of senior researcher at the Space Physics Laboratory of KNU from 1974 to 1990.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nauka.in.ua/en/members/|title=Ukrainian Science Club|website=Ukrainian Science Club}}</ref> During this period, he obtained a [[Doctor of Science]] degree in geophysics from KNU while engaging in space experiments on plasma formations in the [[ionosphere]] and atmospheric clouds via rocket launches from the [[Soviet Union|USSR's]] [[Kapustin Yar]]. He conducted scientific voyages aboard ocean vessels launching meteorological missiles across diverse oceanic regions<ref name=bbb>{{Cite web|url=https://zn.ua/ukr/science/gennadiy-milinevskiy-maye-buti-postiyna-programa-pidtrimki-naukovoyi-molodi-317243_.html|title=Геннадій Міліневський: &quot;Має бути постійна програма підтримки наукової молоді&quot;|website=Зеркало недели &#124; Дзеркало тижня &#124; Mirror Weekly}}</ref> and served as the Base Commander and Geophysicist during the First Ukrainian Antarctic Expedition at the [[Vernadsky Research Base|Vernadsky Station]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://uac.gov.ua/en/the-ukrainian-antarctic-station-is-23-years-old-how-did-everything-happen/|title=The Ukrainian Antarctic station is 23 years old. How did everything happen?|first=Зварич|last=Олена|date=February 5, 2019}}</ref> At Vernadsky Station, his team recorded vital observations for a decade with a focus on [[meteorology]], [[ionospheric sounding]], ozone hole studies, and magnetic measurements.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Investigation of the Vertical Influence of the 11-Year Solar Cycle on Ozone Using SBUV and Antarctic Ground-Based Measurements and CMIP6 Forcing Data|first1=Asen|last1=Grytsai|first2=Oleksandr|last2=Evtushevsky|first3=Andrew|last3=Klekociuk|first4=Gennadi|last4=Milinevsky|first5=Yuri|last5=Yampolsky|first6=Oksana|last6=Ivaniha|first7=Yuke|last7=Wang|date=August 2, 2020|journal=Atmosphere|volume=11|issue=8|pages=873|doi=10.3390/atmos11080873|doi-access=free |bibcode=2020Atmos..11..873G }}</ref>

==Career==
Milinevsky was involved in the transfer of the Faraday Antarctic Base of [[British Antarctic Survey]], UK, to Ukraine and held the position of deputy director of Sciences at the [[National Antarctic Scientific Center of Ukraine]] (NANC) from 1999 to 2006.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ursi.org/files/CommissionWebsites/INAG/web-67/2006/anniversary_ionograms.html|title=11 Jan 2006 ionograms|website=www.ursi.org}}</ref> In 2006, he took the position of head for the Department of Space Physics at KNU, followed by his tenure as the head of the Space Physics Laboratory until 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.americahousekyiv.org/events/2021/6/30-cosmic-solutions-for-a-climate-crisis|title=Cosmic Solutions for a Climate Crisis|date=June 30, 2021|website=America House Kyiv}}</ref> Concurrently, he held the positions of principal scientist of NANC from 2006 to 2023 and participated as a collaborator on the CCMVal Project 42.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pa.op.dlr.de/CCMVal/List_CCMValCollaborators.html|title=CCMVal|website=www.pa.op.dlr.de}}</ref> He was the [[principal investigator]] for the CRDF project UKG2-2969-KV-09 focusing on atmospheric [[aerosol]]s and led international [[AERONET]] sites as well as contributing to the Maritime Aerosol Network (MAN) study, which utilized ''Microtops II sunphotometers''.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://amt.copernicus.org/articles/4/583/2011/|title=Maritime aerosol network as a component of AERONET – first results and comparison with global aerosol models and satellite retrievals|first1=A.|last1=Smirnov|first2=B. ==Research==
Milinevsky has directed his research towards the [[stratosphere]], tropopause, [[ozone layer]], [[ozone depletion]], aerosols, [[Rossby wave|planetary waves]], and [[sudden stratospheric warmings]], alongside exploring space-based techniques and methods for remote sensing of aerosols. His research interests include microwave/millimeter-wave technique used for [[Atmospheric Research|atmosphere research]], climate change processes, and their impact on the ecosystem.<ref name=ble/>

===Atmospheric aerosol===
Milinevsky led the coordination of the Aerosol-UA project in collaboration with the Main Astronomical Observatory which involved installing a polarimeter on a satellite to measure aerosol parameters, including their microphysical and chemical properties in the atmosphere, thereby accurately identifying the location, quantity, and composition of aerosols.<ref name=bbb/> Through a collaborative effort, he contributed to a study that provided an overview of polarimetric observations and their application in characterizing atmospheric aerosols addressing the challenges and achievements in deriving aerosol properties from polarimetric data.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022407318308409|title= Polarimetric remote sensing of atmospheric aerosols: Instruments, methodologies, results, and perspectives|journal=Journal of Quantitative Spectroscopy and Radiative Transfer |date=February 2019 |volume=224 |pages=474–511 |doi=10.1016/j.jqsrt.2018.11.024 |last1=Dubovik |first1=Oleg |last2=Li |first2=Zhengqiang |last3=Mishchenko |first3=Michael I. |last4=Tanré |first4=Didier |last5=Karol |first5=Yana |last6=Bojkov |first6=Bojan |last7=Cairns |first7=Brian |last8=Diner |first8=David J. |last9=Espinosa |first9=W. Reed |last10=Goloub |first10=Philippe |last11=Gu |first11=Xingfa |last12=Hasekamp |first12=Otto |last13=Hong |first13=Jin |last14=Hou |first14=Weizhen |last15=Knobelspiesse |first15=Kirk D. |last16=Landgraf |first16=Jochen |last17=Li |first17=Li |last18=Litvinov |first18=Pavel |last19=Liu |first19=Yi |last20=Lopatin |first20=Anton |last21=Marbach |first21=Thierry |last22=Maring |first22=Hal |last23=Martins |first23=Vanderlei |last24=Meijer |first24=Yasjka |last25=Milinevsky |first25=Gennadi |last26=Mukai |first26=Sonoyo |last27=Parol |first27=Frederic |last28=Qiao |first28=Yanli |last29=Remer |first29=Lorraine |last30=Rietjens |first30=Jeroen |bibcode= 2019JQSRT.224..474D|display-authors=1 |hdl=20.500.12210/105108 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> Furthermore, he investigated the inadvertent cooling effect of the ozone hole formation on inner Antarctica, showcasing how subsequent recovery, vital for ozone restoration, posed challenges by potentially altering atmospheric greenhouse gas dynamics and critical ultraviolet radiation levels essential for life's evolution.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/17/1741/2017/|title=Evolution of the eastward shift in the quasi-stationary minimum of the Antarctic total ozone column|first1=Asen|last1=Grytsai|first2=Andrew|last2=Klekociuk|first3=Gennadi|last3=Milinevsky|first4=Oleksandr|last4=Evtushevsky|first5=Kane|last5=Stone|date=February 3, 2017|journal=Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics|volume=17|issue=3|pages=1741–1758|via=Copernicus Online Journals|doi=10.5194/acp-17-1741-2017|doi-access=free |bibcode=2017ACP....17.1741G |hdl=2440/127273|hdl-access=free}}</ref>

===Environmental research===
Milinevsky as a member of team led by Timothy Mousseau from South Carolina University, has conducted research investigating the effects of radiation exposure within the Chernobyl-contaminated area. Their research on Chernobyl-exposed barn swallows revealed reduced reproduction and survival rates, suggesting significant negative impacts of radioactive contamination on migratory passerines.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1365-2656.2005.01009.x|title=Condition, reproduction and survival of barn swallows from Chernobyl|first1=A. P.|last1=MøLler|first2=T. A.|last2=Mousseau|first3=G.|last3=Milinevsky|first4=A.|last4=Peklo|first5=E.|last5=Pysanets|first6=T.|last6=SzéP|date=November 2, 2005|journal=Journal of Animal Ecology|volume=74|issue=6|pages=1102–1111|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1111/j.1365-2656.2005.01009.x|bibcode=2005JAnEc..74.1102M }}</ref> The later work also revealed that chronic low-dose radiation reduced breeding success in ''Myodes glareolus'' near Chernobyl, with no threshold, and food supplementation benefited only populations in low-radioactive areas, indicating broader ecosystem instability post-nuclear accidents.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://esajournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/ecs2.2667|title=Ecological mechanisms can modify radiation effects in a key forest mammal of Chernobyl|first1=Tapio|last1=Mappes|first2=Zbyszek|last2=Boratyński|first3=Kati|last3=Kivisaari|first4=Anton|last4=Lavrinienko|first5=Gennadi|last5=Milinevsky|first6=Timothy A.|last6=Mousseau|first7=Anders P.|last7=Møller|first8=Eugene|last8=Tukalenko|first9=Phillip C.|last9=Watts|date=April 2, 2019|journal=Ecosphere|volume=10|issue=4|via=CrossRef|doi=10.1002/ecs2.2667|doi-access=free|bibcode=2019Ecosp..10E2667M }}</ref>

In his Antarctic ecology research, Milinevsky examined climate change's effects on [[Antarctic krill]] and ecosystems, highlighting the threat posed by environmental stressors like sea ice decline and ocean warming, emphasizing the need for urgent research and precautionary measures by CCAMLR.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.int-res.com/abstracts/meps/v458/p1-19/|title=Impact of climate change on Antarctic krill|first1=H.|last1=Flores|first2=A.|last2=Atkinson|first3=S.|last3=Kawaguchi|first4=B.
